iconicAnchor.label: Night photography’s graphic universe
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met describes night photography as a graphic universe of shimmering light and velvety darkness, a useful anchor for shape-led tonal contrast.

sources.title: Night Vision: Photography After Dark
supports: Modern photography can derive graphic form from strong relationships between luminous highlights and deep darkness.

sources.title: The Passion of Joan of Arc: four hard-and-fast rules of filmmaking
supports: Plain backgrounds, close framing, and removed depth cues can flatten photographic space into forceful relief-like shape.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches crushed black, blown white, shape first, hard light cut, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/graphic-black-and-white/reference-02.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
